title: Risk and Ruin
blurb: What a loss costs, how deep an ordinary bad run goes, and the fraction that decides whether you survive it.
finding: Risking three per cent a trade rather than one turns a one-in-twenty bad run from 15 per cent of the account into 39.5, which needs a 65 per cent gain to undo.

title: The Cost of Trading
blurb: Everything charged whether the trade works or not, from the spread to the tax, and what each is as a share of your edge.
finding: An index ETF hands over a fifth of one per cent of a typical day’s movement for the right to trade it. A $1.50 micro-cap hands over 52 per cent.

title: Evidence and Proof
blurb: How many trades it takes before a record means anything, and what a backtest is evidence of.
finding: Fifty trades cannot tell a method making 0.35R a trade apart from one with no edge at all. An edge that has halved needs 571.

title: Reading the Book
blurb: What the order book, the tape and the volume actually record, and which parts of them are inferred.
finding: On an ordinary book the quote describes 900 shares out of 7,300, and the aggressor side beside a print is inferred rather than reported.

title: Indicators, Honestly
blurb: What an indicator can and cannot add, how late it is, and what happens when you add a second one.
finding: Three indicators at four lookbacks is twelve configurations and 1.71 independent opinions, and on 20 of 39 bars one reads bullish while another reads bearish.

title: Portfolio and Correlation
blurb: How many independent bets a book of rules is really carrying, and which limit binds before the others.
finding: Two rules on one instrument at the measured correlation carry 1.03 independent bets rather than two, and however many you add the total tops out at 1.06.

title: Trading as a Business
blurb: The pace you actually trade at, the machinery behind it, and the capital a wage requires.
finding: The capital a wage requires is 11.40 years of that wage, and the verdict on whether the edge exists is 10.07 years away at the same pace.

title: Claims Under Test
blurb: The stories the internet tells about charts, each one weighed against what can actually be shown.
finding: On twenty bars the same prices give eight structure events, or two, or none, and the setting that decides is one nobody quotes.

title: Time and the Calendar
blurb: What a bar is a choice about, when the day concentrates its activity, and which of the patterns people hang on the clock survive being measured.
finding: Cut one sixty-bar series into three consecutive twenties and its efficiency ratio reads 0.021, then 0.067, then 0.333 — a sixteenfold spread on a series with no clock, no sessions and one generating rule.
